用 ps、top 看见系统: Observe the system with ps and top
进程是一间独立的房子: A process has its own address space
常见受保护系统中，进程通常拥有各自的虚拟地址空间。: In typical protected systems, processes usually have separate virtual address spaces.
进程通常各有虚拟地址空间，映射由系统管理。: The system manages mappings for each process's address space.
相同地址数值在两个进程中可能对应不同对象。: The same numeric address may refer to different objects in two processes.
交换数据可用管道、套接字或经授权的共享内存等机制。: Pipes, sockets and authorized shared memory can exchange data.
两个进程之间，默认的内存关系是？: What is the default memory relationship between two processes?
各自独立，不能直接互访: Separate spaces, without direct access to each other
由 CPU 型号决定: It depends only on the CPU model
默认隔离的是地址空间；同一数值不能直接当作另一进程对象的指针。系统也可按权限建立: Address spaces are isolated by default. One process's numeric pointer is not directly a pointer to another's object. The OS may establish authorized shared mappings or offer cross-process access interfaces.
线程共享同一间房子里的东西，只是各自有张桌子。: Threads share the same workspace but keep their own execution state.
同一进程的线程通常共享地址空间和进程资源。: Threads in one process usually share its address space and resources.
可共享堆、全局数据及文件描述符等，但访问仍受权限约束。: They can share heap, globals and file descriptors, subject to access permissions.
各线程有寄存器上下文、栈和线程局部状态；栈不是隔离墙。: Each has registers, a stack and thread-local state; a stack is not an isolation wall.
同一进程内的多个线程，默认共享什么？: What do threads in one process normally share?
各自的栈和寄存器: Their register contexts and individual stacks
同一进程线程通常共享地址空间和文件描述符，各有执行上下文和栈。栈内对象的地址也可: Threads usually share an address space and file descriptors while keeping separate contexts and stacks. Another thread may hold a stack object's address, so local variables are not automatically safe.
把读取和更新拆开而缺少同步，可能发生丢失更新。: Unsynchronized read–update sequences can lose updates.
在教学模型中，两个执行者分别读到计数器值10。: In this teaching model, two workers both read counter value 10.
两者各计算11再写回，最后只净增加1。: Each computes 11 and writes it; the net increase is only one.
这是丢失更新示例；具体语言的数据竞争规则还须另看。: This illustrates a lost update; actual data-race rules depend on the language.
按上述读、加、写交错，两者都读到10并写回11，最终值是？: In the stated interleaving, both read 10 and write 11. What is the final value?
一定自动报错: An error is always reported automatically
这个指定交错只留下11，展示丢失更新。不能用该模型预测真实C/C++数据竞争的结: The specified interleaving leaves 11. It does not predict real C/C++ data races, where unsynchronized conflicting accesses may cause undefined behavior.
调度器按策略挑线程，切换时要把现场完整换掉。: The scheduler chooses threads by policy and switches their execution context.
就绪的线程等待处理器，阻塞线程须先等事件满足。: Ready threads wait for a processor; blocked threads first need an event.
调度器依据策略、优先级及运行状况作选择。: Policy, priority and runtime conditions guide scheduling.
切换保存恢复执行上下文；是否换地址空间取决于目标线程。: Switches save and restore context; the target determines whether the address space changes.
多个就绪任务轮转且切换成本不可忽略时，时间片过短可能怎样？: When several ready tasks rotate and switches have a cost, what can very short time slices cause?
上下文切换开销占比变高: A larger proportion of time spent switching contexts
在需要轮转多个就绪任务的条件下，时间片过短可能增加切换开销占比。实际响应和吞吐还: With multiple ready tasks taking turns, shorter slices can increase switching overhead. Actual responsiveness and throughput also depend on policy, load and hardware.
每个进程都以为自己独占内存: Virtual memory gives each process a view
虚拟地址是程序使用的地址，映射和权限决定实际访问。: Programs use virtual addresses; mappings and permissions determine real access.
进程拥有虚拟地址空间，其中可能存在未映射区间。: A virtual address space may include unmapped regions.
地址空间各自组织，也可经授权共享部分物理页。: Separate address spaces can share authorized physical-page mappings.
映射和权限决定访问是否成立，不等于拥有同量物理内存。: An address space does not imply owning an equally large amount of RAM.
虚拟内存带来的好处不包括？: Which is NOT a benefit of virtual memory?
可用地址空间大于物理内存: An address space larger than physical memory
让内存条的物理容量变大: Increasing the physical capacity of RAM modules
虚拟内存不会增加内存条容量。大地址空间可以含未分配区、文件映射或共享页；是否使用: Virtual memory does not add physical RAM. A large address space may contain unallocated regions, file mappings and shared pages. Swap use depends on configuration and page type.
页表关联虚拟页与物理帧，还记录权限等属性。: Page tables map virtual pages to physical frames and record attributes such as permissions.
分页系统按页组织映射；4KiB是常见例子，并非唯一大小。: Paged systems organize mappings in pages; 4 KiB is common, not universal.
页表记录虚拟页到物理帧的映射及权限等信息。: Page tables record mappings and permissions.
TLB可缓存翻译；未命中时才需要进一步查找映射。: A TLB caches translations; misses require further lookup.
页表的作用是什么？: What is a page table's role?
把虚拟页号翻译成物理帧号: Map virtual page numbers to physical frame numbers
页表描述虚拟页映射及权限等属性，TLB帮助缓存翻译。不能把每次内存访问都等同于一: Page tables describe mappings and permissions; the TLB caches translations. Not every memory access performs a full page-table walk.
要用的页不在内存里: When a page is not ready
缺页异常可能用于按需映射，也可能表示非法访问。: Page faults can support demand mapping or signal invalid access.
访问尚未建立有效映射或权限不允许的页，可能触发异常。: Missing mappings or disallowed access may trigger an exception.
系统先检查地址范围、权限和映射类型。: The OS checks the address range, permissions and mapping type.
可恢复时补页或处理写时复制；非法访问则报告错误。: Recoverable faults map pages or handle copy-on-write; invalid access reports an error.
访问合法映射、页面须从后备文件读入且读取成功时，系统会怎样？: For a valid file-backed mapping whose missing page is read successfully, what does the OS do?
调入所需页面、更新映射并重试: Loads the page, updates the mapping and retries
在题目限定的文件后备缺页中，系统调入页面、更新映射并继续执行。另有零填充、写时复: In this file-backed fault, the system loads the page, updates mappings and resumes. Other faults, including zero-fill and copy-on-write, may need no disk read; invalid access may be unrecoverable.
内存压力下会回收页面；频繁回收再访问可能拖慢系统。: Memory pressure triggers page reclaim; repeated reclaim and reuse can slow the system.
系统尝试回收较少使用的页，具体策略依实现而定。: The system tries to reclaim less-used pages with implementation-specific policies.
干净文件页可丢弃后重读；可换出的匿名页可能写交换空间。: Clean file pages can be discarded and reread; eligible anonymous pages may go to swap.
活跃页面反复换入换出或重新读取，可能造成抖动。: Repeatedly swapping or rereading active pages can cause thrashing.
以磁盘换页为主的严重抖动，典型表现是？: What is typical of severe thrashing dominated by disk paging?
CPU 使用率低但磁盘 IO 极高: Low useful CPU activity with very high disk I/O
在该磁盘换页场景中，大量时间用于页面IO，有效计算减少。抖动并不保证每台系统的C: In this scenario, page I/O consumes time and useful computation falls. CPU metrics are not identical on every thrashing system; examine latency, faults and I/O together.
文件其实是张索引卡: A file has metadata and contents
以inode文件系统为例，目录项给名字，inode关联元数据和内容。: In an inode file system, directory entries supply names; inodes describe metadata and contents.
目录项关联文件名与inode编号，不代表所有文件系统都如此。: Entries associate names with inode numbers; not all file systems use this model.
inode保存类型、权限等元数据，并关联文件内容。: An inode holds metadata such as type and permissions and locates contents.
同一文件系统内改名通常更新元数据，不必复制整份内容。: Renaming within one file system usually updates metadata without copying all contents.
同一文件系统内rename普通文件，为何通常不用复制全部内容？: Why does renaming a regular file within one file system usually avoid copying its contents?
因为会复制一份数据: Because it duplicates all the data
主要更新目录项和相关元数据: It mainly updates directory entries and related metadata
同一文件系统的rename通常调整名字关联及相关元数据，不搬动整份内容。跨文件系: A same-file-system rename typically changes name associations and metadata, not all data. Cross-file-system rename may fail; a tool such as mv can instead copy and delete.
在inode模型中，目录提供名字到文件对象的查找关系。: In the inode model, a directory provides lookup from names to file objects.
目录也有元数据和目录内容，具体布局依文件系统而定。: Directories have metadata and contents; layout depends on the file system.
目录项关联名字与inode等对象标识。: Entries connect names to identifiers such as inode numbers.
解析路径会检查目录、权限及链接等，缓存可减少实际IO。: Path resolution checks directories, permissions and links; caches can reduce I/O.
解析普通路径/docs/a.md以打开文件时，系统主要做什么？: What primarily happens when opening /docs/a.md through ordinary path resolution?
直接按名字找数据块: The name directly selects data blocks
逐级解析目录项并取得目标文件对象: Directory entries are resolved step by step to find the file object
把文件全部读进内存: All file contents are read into memory
路径解析找出目标对象并进行访问检查，打开文件不等于立刻读取全部内容。缓存、符号链: Path resolution finds the target and checks access. Opening does not mean immediately reading all contents. Caches, symbolic links and mount points also affect resolution.
文件被切成块存: Files can be allocated in blocks
按块分配是常见模型，块大小和实际占用要看文件系统。: Block allocation is common; block size and actual space use depend on the file system.
以4KiB块分配为例，文件内容可以分布在多个块。: With 4 KiB blocks, file contents can span multiple blocks.
元数据记录内容位置，可能用区段等方式组织。: Metadata locates contents, sometimes using extents.
碎片对机械盘和SSD的影响不同，不能统一保证减速幅度。: Fragmentation affects HDDs and SSDs differently; no single slowdown is guaranteed.
按4KiB独立分配块且无内联或压缩时，1字节内容为何占一个块？: With independent 4 KiB blocks and no inline data or compression, why does one byte occupy a block?
分配单位为4KiB，余量形成块内空闲: Allocation uses 4 KiB units, leaving unused space within the block
因为磁盘有冗余备份: Because the drive keeps redundant backups
题目限定的模型按块分配，内容不足一块仍占该块。真实文件系统可能支持内联、压缩等特: In the stated model, even sub-block contents use a full block. Real file systems may use inline data or compression; metadata also consumes space.
断电时别把账本撕坏: Keep structures consistent after a crash
日志帮助崩溃后恢复结构一致性，不等于所有数据都已持久化。: Journaling helps recover structural consistency; it does not mean all data is durable.
一次更新可能涉及多处元数据，需要协调一致。: One update can touch several metadata locations that must agree.
日志记录事务，恢复时处理已经提交的记录。: A journal records transactions; recovery processes committed records.
数据是否走日志和何时落盘，取决于文件系统及模式。: Data journaling and persistence timing depend on the file system and mode.
文件系统日志（journal）主要解决什么问题？: What does file-system journaling primarily address?
断电后能恢复到一致状态: Recovering a consistent state after power loss
日志主要帮助恢复一致的文件系统结构，但不保证最近写入都已保存，也不能替代备份、正: Journaling helps restore consistent structures. It does not guarantee all recent writes survived, or replace backups, correct synchronization and failure checks.
九位分三组，分别对应所有者、同组、其他人。: Three groups represent owner, group and others.
权限串共十位，第一位是文件类型，d 表示目录。: In the ten-character display, the first character is type; d means directory.
后面九位分三组；普通文件 rwx 是读、写、执行，目录则是列名、修改目录项、搜索: File rwx means read, write, execute; directory rwx means list, change entries, search.
缺哪个权限就用短横占位，位置不能省。: A missing permission uses a dash; positions cannot be omitted.
普通文件权限 rw-r--r-- 表示什么？: What does rw-r--r-- mean for a regular file?
所有者读写，其他人都只读: The owner may read and write; others may only read
第一组 rw- 是所有者可读写，后两组 r-- 都只读；换成数字就是 644。: Owner rw- grants read/write; both r-- groups grant read only. Numerically, this is 644.
基本权限位按进程身份选择所有者、同组或其他人规则。: Basic permissions select owner, group or others according to process identity.
只看基本权限位时，先比较进程身份与文件所有者。: First compare process identity with the file owner.
若不是所有者，再比较文件组与进程的有效组及附加组。: If not the owner, compare the file group with effective and supplementary groups.
都不匹配时使用其他人位；ACL和特权等条件另行判断。: Otherwise use others. ACLs, privileges and other policies also matter.
只按基本权限位，非特权进程既非所有者也不匹配文件组，使用哪组？: Under basic permission bits, which class applies to an unprivileged process matching neither owner nor group?
在题目限定的基本权限模型中使用其他人位，不从三组中取最大值。实际访问还可能涉及A: The stated basic model uses others, not the most permissive set. Actual access may also involve ACLs, path-search permissions, privilege and other security policies.
通常所有者可改权限；改变所有者需要相应特权。: Owners can usually change mode; changing ownership needs appropriate privilege.
chmod设置权限位，也可涉及setuid、setgid等特殊位。: chmod sets permission bits, including special bits such as setuid and setgid.
chown调整所有者或所属组，权限条件并不完全相同。: chown changes owner or group, with different permission conditions.
Linux普通非特权进程不能任意更改文件所有者。: An ordinary unprivileged Linux process cannot arbitrarily change file owners.
普通用户能把文件的所属权转给另一个用户吗？: Can an ordinary user transfer file ownership to another user?
不行，通常需要 root 权限: No; it normally requires root-level privilege
可以，只要文件是空的: Yes, if the file is empty
以Linux为例，任意改变所有者需要CAP_CHOWN等相应特权，通常由特权管理: On Linux, arbitrary owner changes require privilege such as CAP_CHOWN, normally through privileged administration. Having that capability is not identical to requiring the username root.
高权限服务被攻破后，攻击者通常能直接影响更多资源。: A compromised privileged service can usually directly affect more resources.
Linux把许多特权拆为capabilities，UID为0不等于无限放行。: Linux splits many privileges into capabilities; UID 0 is not unlimited access.
实际权限还受能力集合、命名空间及安全策略等约束。: Capability sets, namespaces and security policies constrain actual powers.
服务使用专用身份和必要权限，可减少直接暴露的资源。: Dedicated identities with only needed permissions limit direct exposure.
为什么 Web 服务不建议用 root 运行？: Why is running a web service as root discouraged?
被攻破后可能直接获得更广的操作权限: Compromise may directly grant broader access
减少服务权限通常能限制攻击者可直接操作的资源，但提权漏洞或其他凭证泄漏仍可能扩大: Lower privilege usually limits directly accessible resources, though escalation bugs or leaked credentials can widen damage. UID 0 inside a container does not automatically grant all host powers.
shell 也只是个程序: A shell is a program too
以POSIX风格shell为例，它解析命令并执行内置命令或程序。: A POSIX-style shell parses commands and runs built-ins or external programs.
shell解析命令、展开和重定向，并查找要执行的内容。: It parses commands, expansions and redirections, then finds what to execute.
外部命令通常在子进程中执行；内置命令可在shell中执行。: External commands usually run in child processes; built-ins can run in the shell.
前台命令通常等待完成，后台命令和exec等情况不同。: Foreground commands usually wait for completion; background jobs and exec differ.
shell把ls解析为外部程序并在前台执行时，通常会怎样？: When a shell resolves ls as an external foreground program, what usually happens?
自己实现了列目录功能: The shell implements directory listing itself
找到 ls 程序，创建子进程执行它: It finds ls and creates a child process to run it
把命令发给显示器: It sends the command to the display
常见实现创建子进程、执行找到的ls并等待它结束。内置命令、函数、后台任务或exe: Typical shells create a child, execute the located ls and wait for completion. Built-ins, functions, background jobs and exec behave differently; not every command creates a process.
ps 给的是某一刻的快照，top 则持续刷新。: ps gives a snapshot; top refreshes over time.
PID标识当前PID命名空间中的进程，结束后编号可能复用。: A PID identifies a process in its PID namespace and may later be reused.
Linux procps示例：R为运行或就绪，S为可中断睡眠，Z为僵尸。: Linux procps: R means running/ready, S interruptible sleep, Z zombie.
top持续采样刷新，可切换排序；输出不是全系统同时刻快照。: top refreshes samples and can change sorting; it is not an instantaneous whole-system view.
进程状态 Z（僵尸）意味着什么？: What does process state Z, or zombie, mean?
进程正在满负荷运行: The process is running at full load
进程已结束，等父进程回收退出状态: Execution ended; its parent must reap the exit status
进程在等待网络: The process is waiting for networking
僵尸已结束执行，但退出状态等少量信息尚待父进程或收养者回收。它并非还在执行任务，: A zombie has stopped executing; a small amount of information, including exit status, awaits its parent or adopter. It is not still doing work and normally no longer holds its old user address space.
普通管道把前一命令的标准输出接到后一命令的标准输入。: An ordinary pipe connects one command's standard output to the next command's standard input.
标准输入、标准输出和标准错误是常用的三个流。: stdin, stdout and stderr are three common streams.
普通竖线连接stdout到stdin，不自动合并stderr。: A normal pipe joins stdout to stdin without automatically merging stderr.
常见重定向中>截断后写入、>>追加；具体行为还受选项影响。: Typically > truncates and writes, while >> appends; options can affect behavior.
命令 a | b 中，竖线的作用是？: What does the pipe in a | b do?
把两条命令合并成一个程序: Merges both commands into one program
把a的标准输出接到b的标准输入: Connects a's stdout to b's stdin
把a的结果存成文件: Saves a's output to a file
让b等a结束再启动: Waits for a to exit before starting b
普通管道连接标准输出与标准输入，标准错误另行处理。两端通常可并发工作，但缓冲和阻: Ordinary pipes connect stdout to stdin; stderr is separate. Both ends can usually run concurrently, though buffering and blocking affect when data is consumed.
kill发送信号；权限、信号种类和进程状态决定后续行为。: Permissions, signal type and process state determine what follows a signal.
以常见Unix信号为例：TERM、INT、KILL各有用途。: Common Unix signals include TERM, INT and KILL, each with a role.
TERM默认终止，也可被程序捕获处理或忽略。: TERM terminates by default but can be handled or ignored.
KILL不能捕获、阻塞或忽略，不给应用执行收尾处理的机会。: KILL cannot be caught, blocked or ignored and gives no application cleanup opportunity.
kill -9 和 kill -15 的关键区别是？: What is the key difference between kill -9 and kill -15?
-9 不可被捕获，进程无法清理；-15 可被处理: -9 cannot be caught for cleanup; -15 can be handled
以常见Unix编号为例，SIGKILL不能被捕获；SIGTERM可被处理。发送成: With common Unix numbering, SIGKILL cannot be caught; SIGTERM can be handled. Successfully sending a signal does not guarantee immediate exit. Graceful shutdown depends on implemented and completed cleanup.
